hyps.why: Node 1 is dead when edge 0 is none, so a conv on 1->2 has no input and no effect.
A dead node 1 makes the 1->3 conv inert.
A dead node 1 makes a conv on 1->2 inert.
Replacing none with a conv reconnects node 2 to the output, a much larger gain than upgrading another op.
Activating an empty 1->3 edge with a conv gains more than replacing an existing op.
Giving the output a direct learned path from the input is a large gain when the edge was empty.
Adding a learnable path where there was none is a clear gain.
Restoring a learnable connection to the output beats the average replacement.
Adding a conv on an empty 1->2 edge creates a new learnable path, more than replacing an existing op.
Edge 0 being none disables node 1, so adding a conv activates edges 2 and 4 and gains a lot.
